projects.title: District 7: Subterranean Neon
projects.subtitle: Cyberpunk Parkour & Combat Sandbox
projects.summary: A high-speed parkour and combat sandbox set in a vertically stacked cyberpunk bazaar. Engineered fluid wall-running verbs and responsive grapple physics, while leveraging real-time neon emissive lighting to intuitively guide player pathfinding at 60 FPS.
projects.creativeIntent: Marry high-agility gameplay mechanics with subconscious lighting wayfinding. Warm orange neon signs highlight interactive mantle ledges, while cold cyan emissives mark stealth flanking routes without cluttering the screen with UI markers.
projects.technicalChallenge: Maintaining 60 FPS on current-gen consoles under 14 dynamic emissive light meshes, dense volumetric fog passes, and high-frequency roughness reflections across puddles.
projects.solution: Engineered a custom Lumen GI bounce hierarchy with prioritized screen-space traces, decoupled dynamic light culling at 35m bounds, and tuned roughness thresholds to eradicate specular fireflies.

gameplayDesign.encounterPacing: High-intensity 45-second parkour traversal interspersed with 360-degree arena combat encounters
gameplayDesign.feelAndJuice: Impact frames on hard landings, variable camera FOV kick on wall-runs, and responsive haptic audio rumble

projects.subtitle: Competitive Tactical Arena Blockout

projects.technicalChallenge: Preventing dominant camping positions while rewarding coordinated team rotation between upper catwalks and lower perimeter ditches.
projects.solution: Designed 4 distinct flanking angles for every primary strongpoint, calibrated cover heights strictly to 1.1m (crouch) and 2.0m (full cover), and color-coded team navigation routes.

projects.title: The Ossuary of Sanctors
projects.subtitle: Gothic Stealth-Horror Sanctuary
projects.summary: A gothic stealth-horror dungeon where light and darkness act as primary game mechanics. Players must time patrol stealth around dynamic fire braziers and pale lunar shafts, using shadows for concealment and light for sanctuary.
projects.creativeIntent: Turn lighting into an active gameplay antagonist and ally. Moonlight shafts expose player silhouettes to wandering inquisitors, while flickering oil braziers define safe pockets for health and stamina recovery.
projects.technicalChallenge: Simulating realistic fire flicker and dynamic torch shadows in vaulted stone ceilings without incurring massive GPU shadow map draw calls.
projects.solution: Utilized virtual shadow maps (VSM) with clamped high-frequency light radii, paired with procedural material vertex displacement on flames and light function flicker curves.

gameplayDesign.coreLoop: Stalk Shadows → Observe AI Torch Sweep Paths → Dash Between Moonlight Pillars → Purge Shrine Relic → Evade Cathedral Hunt
gameplayDesign.progressionEconomy: Tallow candles act as consumable light sources, burned to open sealed crypt portals
gameplayDesign.encounterPacing: Deliberate survival horror tension with heartbeat pacing curves and sudden ambush spikes
gameplayDesign.feelAndJuice: Screen-edge vignette darkness, dynamic vignette bloom when entering safe sanctuary light, and muffled audio in shadows

projects.title: Derelict Station: Apollo Zero
projects.subtitle: Zero-G Orbital Survival Mechanics
projects.summary: A suspense zero-G survival experience where intermittent rotating crimson beacons serve as rhythmic puzzle and navigation beats. Players memorize corridor layout during strobe flashes before zero-gravity propulsion drift.
projects.creativeIntent: Harness sensory deprivation and periodic visual information as core gameplay mechanics. Players must make high-consequence spatial navigation choices during momentary bursts of illumination.
projects.technicalChallenge: Real-time rotating spot lights with high-intensity bounce in reflective brushed metallic corridors without inducing temporal ghosting in Lumen.
projects.solution: Constructed custom light attenuation profiles, tuned temporal super-resolution (TSR) anti-ghosting flags, and clamped specular indirect clamp values.

projects.title: Titan Orbital Rail Turret
projects.subtitle: Kinetic Weapon Systems & PBR Look-Dev
projects.summary: An interactive modular orbital defense turret prototype featuring mechanical firing loops, recoil animation states, and thermal heat management, presented with studio-grade PBR look-dev lighting.
projects.creativeIntent: Emphasize the mechanical mass, lethal precision, and player feedback loops through sculpted softbox rim highlights and sharp specular reflections along beveled armor edges.

projects.solution: Implemented calibrated GGX microfacet distribution with anisotropy channels, paired with physical camera shutter and aperture settings.

profile.name: Avinash
profile.title: Game Designer | Lighting Artist
profile.headline: Designing Gameplay, Mechanics and Living Worlds.
profile.leadCopy: Professional Game Designer specializing in core gameplay loops, mechanics, player pacing, and level architecture — powered by a lifelong hobby and passion as a Lighting Artist.
profile.philosophyText: When a Game Designer understands light transport, they do not need arbitrary floating objective arrows or artificial mini-map clutter. Contrast draws the crosshair, warmth signals safe recharge zones, silhouette breaks frame enemy weakpoints, and console frametimes remain protected because gameplay geometry and lighting budgets are planned together.

siteContent.heroHeadline: Designing Gameplay, Mechanics and Living Worlds.
siteContent.heroLeadCopy: My profession is Game Design: engineering intuitive gameplay mechanics, systemic loops, combat pacing, and spatial architecture that make games unforgettable to play, combined with my dedicated creative passion as a Lighting Artist. This dual superpower bridges player psychology with cinematic visual atmosphere.
siteContent.studioDescription: Take the director's chair in my lighting passion lab. Adjust key light angles, tweak sky bounce, toggle between PBR Lit and Clay passes, and inspect how light sculpts spatial geometry and player sightlines in real time.

siteContent.levelHeadline: Core Mechanics, Combat Loops & Spatial Pacing
siteContent.levelDescription: Great game design balances player agency, mechanical depth, and intuitive guidance. Here is how core loops, encounter spaces, and player feedback systems are architected from paper to engine.
siteContent.levelCard1Desc: Designing responsive character verbs, combat timing windows, risk/reward resource economies, and satisfying feedback feel. Iterating continuously on controller response and mechanical clarity.
siteContent.levelCard2Desc: Architecting tension-and-release pacing curves, asymmetric multiplayer cover geometry, and 3-lane combat arenas. Calibrating sightline buffers and verticality to create dynamic tactical choices.
siteContent.levelCard3Desc: Leveraging my passion for lighting to reinforce game design goals: subconscious focal beacons, silhouette contrast for threat identification, and zero-HUD spatial navigation that keeps players immersed.
siteContent.aboutLead: My profession is Game Design: crafting intuitive gameplay mechanics, systemic loops, combat pacing, and spatial architecture that make games unforgettable to play. My lifelong hobby and creative passion is lighting art. This dual perspective allows me to design levels and mechanics where lighting is not an afterthought, but an active gameplay tool that guides, warns, and rewards the player.
